Wheat - Mite.remedy: Apply sulfur-based acaricides. Avoid water stress which worsens mite outbreaks. Encourage natural predators.
Wheat - Mite.conditions: Thrives in hot (28-38°C) and dry conditions; drought-stressed crops are most vulnerable.

Wheat - Powdery Mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces and stems; affected leaves turn yellow and die.
Wheat - Powdery Mildew.remedy: Apply triadimefon or propiconazole fungicides. Use resistant varieties. Avoid high nitrogen and dense planting.
Wheat - Powdery Mildew.conditions: Favored by cool to mild (15-22°C) temperatures with high humidity but no free water on leaves.

Wheat - Septoria.symptoms: Pale brown irregular blotches with yellow margins on leaves; tiny black pycnidia visible in lesions.
Wheat - Septoria.remedy: Apply azoxystrobin or propiconazole. Use certified clean seed. Destroy crop residue post-harvest.
Wheat - Septoria.conditions: Thrives in cool (10-20°C) and wet conditions; rain splash moves spores up the canopy progressively.

Wheat - Smut.symptoms: Grain heads replaced by black powdery masses of fungal spores; infected plants may be slightly taller.
Wheat - Smut.remedy: Treat seeds with carboxin or thiram before sowing. Use smut-resistant varieties. Remove infected heads before spore release.
Wheat - Smut.conditions: Seed-borne infection occurring at germination; cool (5-20°C) and moist soil conditions favor infection.

Wheat - Stem Fly.symptoms: Dead central shoots (deadhearts) at tillering; larvae found inside stem at base.
Wheat - Stem Fly.remedy: Apply chlorpyrifos or imidacloprid at tillering. Sow early to avoid peak fly activity. Remove and destroy affected tillers.
Wheat - Stem Fly.conditions: Pest activity peaks in warm (20-30°C) conditions during early crop stages; late sowing increases vulnerability.

Wheat - Tan Spot.symptoms: Tan to brown oval lesions with yellow halos; lesions may coalesce causing large blighted areas.
Wheat - Tan Spot.remedy: Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole. Rotate with non-cereal crops. Incorporate or burn stubble to reduce inoculum.
Wheat - Tan Spot.conditions: Thrives in warm (20-28°C) and wet conditions; stubble from previous crops is the primary inoculum source.

Wheat - Yellow Rust.symptoms: Bright yellow pustules arranged in stripes along leaves; white to pale yellow in cool conditions.
Wheat - Yellow Rust.remedy: Apply propiconazole or tebuconazole at first sign. Use resistant varieties. Monitor during cool humid weather.
Wheat - Yellow Rust.conditions: Favored by cool (10-15°C) and moist conditions; most active in early spring with heavy dew or light rainfall.
